title: Chaff & Core Clause Pocket Log
content:
Purpose: quick personal pocket log for negotiation signals, minimal fallback language, and a fast risk scoring heuristic when triaging early-stage deals. Intended for my own use during redlines; keep terse.

Top-of-mind clauses to flag (quick scan checklist):
- Indemnity: caps, carve-outs for third-party claims that arise from model outputs, crypto/excluded risks. Flag if uncapped or insurer-unfriendly.
- IP assignment vs license: who owns derivatives of customer data + model outputs? Prefer narrow license + customer retention of customer-supplied data.
- Data use / training rights: avoid blanket "may use" for training unless anonymized & opt-in. Prefer: limited aggregation + purpose-bound telemetry.
- Hallucination liability: customers often ask for remedies — push to disclaimer + operational SLOs, not warranties.
- Escrow & export controls: if escrow requested, ask why (regulatory vs commercial). Export clauses need commodity-control checks for certain models.
- Termination & transition: require data export window and a trained-runbook for private infra. Ask for SLA for handover support if they ask for termination assistance.
- Security breach notice timing: 72 hrs is aggressive; aim for 10 business days unless PII involved.
- Discovery / audit rights: narrow to specific, infrequent audits with JIRA/PR-triggered scope.
- Subpoena / government requests: require notice where lawful and strict minimization.
- Warranty period: keep short (30–90 days) for deliverables; for API uptime use SLA credits not indemnities.

Quick risk scoring (30-second):
- Score 1-5 on each: Financial exposure, Reputational exposure, Regulatory complexity, Operational burden.
- Redline threshold: if Financial >=4 OR Regulatory >=4 -> escalate to lead counsel.

Negotiation playbook (short scripts):
- If counterparty asks for broad training rights: "We can provide telemetry and aggregated insights for service improvement but cannot grant rights to retrain our models on customer data. We can discuss a narrow, opt-in corpus process with controls."
- If they insist on uncapped indemnity: "We need to align on a commercial cap tied to the annual contract value; uncapped indemnities require legal escalation and insurance review. Is there a specific claim you're protecting against?"
- On IP assignment asks: "We don't do assignment of core model IP. We can assign customer-created outputs under a license or provide a transfer of customer-supplied models under specific terms."

Alternative clause templates (boilerplate I reach for):
- Limited training rights (proposal): "Provider may use Customer Data solely to improve and operate the Services in aggregated, de-identified form and not to create a model derivative that is substantially similar to Customer Data. Any use for model training will be subject to a separate written agreement."

- Hallucination / output warranty carve (proposal): "Provider does not warrant that generated outputs are factually correct. Provider will maintain reasonable operational processes and will use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize material output defects. Customer remedies for material, reproducible defects are limited to re-processing or service credits."

- Indemnity cap language (proposal): "Provider's aggregate liability and indemnity obligations shall not exceed the fees paid by Customer under the Order in the 12 months preceding the claim. Neither party shall be liable for indirect, incidental, or consequential damages."

Escalation triggers (flag and ping):
- Any request for uncapped indemnity OR express insurance requirement beyond standard limits -> escalate to Liam + insurance broker.
- Any clause that gives customer rights to retrain models on our internal weights or to receive our model weights -> immediate red flag, escalate to engineering + research.
- Export control or military use language -> escalate to compliance.

Tactical concessions I can make quickly (low-friction):
- Add a 12-month sunset on data-use permission for training.
- Agree to a held-in-escrow copy of customer configs (not model binaries) for transition.
- Provide a 30-day notice window for planned model architecture changes that materially impact API shape.

Non-starters (need C-level sign-off):
- Assignment of model IP to customer.
- Uncapped punitive damages tied to model outputs.
- Authority for customer to perform unbounded continuous audits into our production environment.

Notes to self / reminders:
- When they ask for "source code access" clarify: we can offer function-level hooks, but not training-time weights or proprietary kernels.
- For Dedicated/Private deals: add an ops-runbook SLA (hand-off checklist + runbook fee if required).
- Prep evidence pack (prior to escalation): attach insurance certificate, past incident post-mortem redaction, and a sample runbook.

Open questions to tidy before next negotiation:
- What is current carve for "model improvements" in our standard TOS? (check contract-templates PR #87)
- Insurance: what's our standard limits and can we extend to 10M for enterprise? (ask Liam)
- Any recent claims that inform our indemnity posture? (ask Sofia for redacted examples)

Quick links / shorthand to use in threads: 
- PR #87 = template language for training-rights 
- JIRA AI-3421 = customer X escalation (notes in Confluence)
- Slack legal-private = quick ping for 1:1 review

End-of-log: keep this short and iterative. Delete or split into deal-specific notes once a negotiation completes. 

Scratchy bits (raw ideas):
- Consider a small addendum standard: "output-acceptance test" (customer supplies 20 canonical prompts; if >X% hallucination -> remediation plan) — could be a sellable QA add-on.
- For public sector deals, push for two-tiered training rights (none for default, limited for explicit consent + procurement route).
